# 🔏 SPN-149 — revocation closure across navigation

## 🧭 Registration and scope

Date: 2026-11-12. Status: owner-approved backlog registration, implementation and
runtime verification pending. The owner approved the grooming recommendations in
chat (“Yes perfect, thank you.”). [Full audit](grooming-2026-11-12.md).

Merged [PR #268](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/pull/268) preserves
[main run 42329786250 / job 128273632504](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/actions/runs/42329786250/job/128273632504):
the session-revocation check counted zero Playwright WebSocket-close events
within five seconds although its first-attempt DOM showed sign-in. The later
surviving-login queued-edit and broadcast assertions had not run. Retry passed
but correctly failed the flaky-test gate; only that retry retained a trace.
A later complete first attempt passed in 4,848 ms. The original event ordering
remains unavailable, and the restore correction in #268 did not repair it.

The PR's source inspection supports navigation clearing Playwright's socket map
as a hypothesis. Current `e2e/collaboration.spec.ts`, in
“revoking one login preserves another login’s queued edit and stops later broadcasts”,
directly revokes one session, then counts page WebSocket-close events before
releasing the other login's queued write. Missing observer
events alone do not prove retained authorization or a security defect.

Choose a distinct **M, pre-launch** investigation instead of relying on unrelated
passes or silently expanding SPN-120's finite historical cases. Scope includes
current socket/session/navigation inspection, one declared bounded experiment,
a demonstrated fixture correction and focused negative controls, then the actual
browser security journey. Reassess before product/session or protocol work.
Stop at the declared sample limit and preserve any inconclusive/not-reproduced
disposition; this cannot waive a failed current-head gate or claim the original
ordering was proved.

Operator gains trustworthy revocation evidence. Owner and Collaborator retain
socket termination, request denial and saved-work/session-continuity proof.
Link guest's separate capability/revocation controls stay intact, with only an
indirect test-quality benefit. No authentication policy or authority is changed
by this registration; SPN-145's service-worker investigation remains separate.

## 🔎 Verification checkpoint

Independent grooming review corrected the initial passkey-test attribution to
this exact two-login collaboration case. The title now says session revocation;
the approved incident and bounded outcome are unchanged. Passkey-management
coverage is related regression protection, not the source of this recorded failure.

No new experiment has run. Record hypothesis, source/runtime, fixed first-attempt
count, resource bounds and stop condition before execution. Prove a live socket
and active authorization still fail, and retain editor removal, surviving-login
continuity, successful queued writes from the surviving login, no later broadcasts and saved/reloaded content.
A sign-in screen alone cannot establish closure. Keep current deadlines and
privacy-safe first-failure/cleanup evidence; no retry-to-green or deleted assertion.

## 🧪 Declared investigation — 2026-11-12

Agent decision under the owner's ticket-specific authorization. Complete outcome
remains M: one observation-boundary correction, focused controls, the existing
two-login journey, and its unchanged hosted acceptance. Product authentication,
transport policy and navigation behavior are outside this correction.

**Falsifiable hypothesis:** Playwright's page-level close observation loses a
previously established socket when main-frame new-document navigation clears its
socket map before the protocol close notification is dispatched. A request-ID
observer attached directly to Chromium's Network events should retain the actual
close independently of that map. Navigation without a close must remain failure.

**Source and runtime declared before execution:** current main
`04baabd6a68abe7c0b225f8699681532e2205b60`; Node `26.13.0`, executable SHA-256
`0adde40d1b7dfa57c8bc83cbc319758c3ec6ebba21363bb2fa752ea6b267ad1b`;
lockfile SHA-256 `cdb5afd5811c7229c9b0c9ffd945a51848dd1c58b32051d1fb20d2842568177c`;
Playwright `1.64.1`, installed `coreBundle.js` SHA-256
`829521b67ed7be90c7d6d6098ff39f2241562d47e4ad7ccab13710924a56001d`.
The original browser and the unchanged pinned hosted owner are Chromium
`156.0.8078.4`, revision `1248`. Record the complete candidate and tested-merge
identities before/with hosted execution; never substitute this base for them.

**Fixed sample and stop condition:** one browser-free dispatch probe of the
installed Playwright runtime, with exactly two controlled orderings: close before
main-frame map clearing, then clearing before close. This deliberately injected
ordering can demonstrate the observer boundary, not the historical browser's
ordering or real server closure. Stop after both orderings or the first probe
error. Then use exactly the existing development and production Chromium
two-login cases, once each at retry zero in the first reviewed candidate's hosted
run. Retain every configured retry separately; a retry cannot replace a failed
first attempt. If neither native case exhibits the ordering, record the natural
recurrence as not reproduced. Do not add a repeat matrix or run until green.

**Bounds:** one local workload at a time via `scripts/serial.ts`, a process-tree
RSS watchdog capped at 2 GiB and eight minutes, with system pressure checked
before and during work. The browser-free probe has a 10-second outer bound.
The actual journey keeps its 60-second test deadline, five-second closure poll,
existing save/readiness deadlines, and `failOnFlakyTests`. New diagnostics store
only finite event kinds, relative times, counts and statuses; no socket URLs,
tickets, cookies, identifiers, frame payloads or authored content.

**Capability checkpoint:** pinned dependencies installed successfully under the
watchdog (peak 1,182,360 KiB, 11.967 s). Pinned Chromium local installation failed:
the official installer downloaded invalid/empty ZIPs on its five built-in
attempts. No local browser case ran and this is not passing acceptance. Keep
browser execution with the existing hosted owners, without substituting another
browser version or changing the environment matrix.

Operator gains durable, bounded first-attempt evidence. Owner and Collaborator
keep denial, real closure, the surviving login's queued write and saved/reloaded
content as separate assertions. Link guest authorization and journeys are
unchanged. No server/session defect is inferred from a missing observer event.
limitation: Local pre-execution declaration, retained verbatim; not a record of the missing historical first-attempt browser timeline.
